_doc: Taint semantics for external/library functions consumed by the bn taint engine. Keys are symbol names (leading underscores / common decorations are stripped when matching). Grammar for from/to: 'arg:N' = value of the Nth (0-based) argument, '*arg:N' = the buffer the Nth argument points to (its pointee variable), 'ret' = return value, '*ret' = pointee of returned pointer. 'sources' seed taint; 'propagates' move taint from->to when 'from' is tainted; 'sink.tainted_args' lists argument indices whose taint is reportable, with a 'class' bug-class hint. Keys beginning with '_' are ignored. A user override at the path from paths.taint_models_path() is merged over these.

models._comment_return_bound: return_bound.max_from_arg N: the return value (bytes received) is provably <= the constant in arg N (the count). Lets forward taint downgrade `m = read(fd,buf,MAX); memcpy(dst,buf,m)` from overflow to bounded_len with source_bound=MAX (#159).
models._comment_recv_overflow: read/recv/recvfrom(fd, buf, len): the length (arg2) written into buf (arg1) can overflow an undersized destination. Modeled as an OPT-IN bounded-write sink gated behind `--sink-class recv_overflow` -- NOT always-on: a firmware measurement (#499) found ~100% false positives, because the dominant idiom `n = read(fd, buf+progress, cap-progress)` derives its length from the call's own return-value source, so the sink arms itself on a provably-bounded length. Enable it only when deliberately hunting recv-into-fixed-buffer overflows; the finding still reports class `overflow_len`.

sink.detail: attacker-controlled length written into buf via read()
attacker-controlled length written into buf via recv()
attacker-controlled length written into buf via recvfrom()

models._comment_recvmsg: recvmsg/recvmmsg scatter the received bytes into the iovec buffers at arg1->msg_iov[i].iov_base (recvmmsg: arg1[0].msg_hdr.msg_iov...), NOT a direct buffer arg. '*iovec:N' resolves the msghdr at arg N through the statically-set msg_iov and iov_base fields to the filled buffer(s) (#306); when the iovec setup can't be resolved the seeder falls back to an honest nudge.
models._comment_fgetc: Byte-at-a-time file/stream sources (CWE-121-style hand-rolled token/parse loops). Without these, fgetc/getc/getchar are unmodeled calls and a hand-rolled `while ((c = fgetc(f)) != EOF) buf[i++] = c;` loop shows only coarse_memory_store leaves with no modeled source in the catalog. Each returns a single int (the byte read or EOF) -- seed the return value, not a buffer arg.

sink.detail: unbounded copy of tainted source into strcpy dest
unbounded append of tainted source into strcat dest

models._comment_extra_copy: BSD/glibc copy primitives beyond the classic libc set (previously enumerated by the retired sink-sweep.sh, now modeled so `bn taint models` and the engine cover them). bcopy has REVERSED args vs memcpy -- bcopy(src, dst, n) -- so it propagates *arg:0 -> *arg:1 and its length is arg 2. mempcpy mirrors memcpy. strlcpy/strlcat are size-bounded like strncpy/strncat: a tainted size arg is the overflow sink.

sink.detail: attacker-controlled length to bcopy (src, dst, n)

models._comment_format_v: Plain (non-_chk) v-printf family + asprintf/dprintf (#317): the unfortified libc formatters that an internal vformatter wrapper bottoms out at -- previously only the _chk/_s variants were modeled, so a tainted format routed through e.g. a `gs_snprintf` wrapper calling plain vsnprintf passed through unflagged. v* take a va_list (no discoverable varargs); the format-string arg is the sink.
models._comment_format_chk: Fortified printf-family: leading flag/strlen (and maxlen for snprintf) args shift the format string + varargs right. v* take a va_list (no discoverable varargs), so no 'varargs'.
models._comment_asprintf_chk: FORTIFY asprintf/vasprintf (#373): __asprintf_chk(strp, flags, fmt, ...) and __vasprintf_chk(strp, flags, fmt, va_list). The leading `flags` arg shifts the format string to arg2 (vs arg1 in the plain asprintf/vasprintf above). asprintf has real varargs from arg3; vasprintf takes a va_list (no discoverable varargs).

sink.detail: tainted path to dlopen() (arbitrary library load)

models._comment_cxx_new: C++ operator new / new[] (Itanium ABI). Keyed underscore-stripped (Znwm/Znam) so the mangled symbols resolve via lookup_model, which also canonicalizes the size_t-overload (Znwm/Znwj), nothrow/aligned suffixes, and the demangled 'operator new'/'operator new[]' spellings to these two keys (#204). Like malloc, the size is arg 0. Placement new (_ZnwmPv / 'operator new(size, void*)') does not allocate and is excluded by lookup_model, so it never reaches here.

sink.detail: attacker-controlled allocation size to operator new
attacker-controlled allocation size to operator new[]

models._comment_fortified: FORTIFY_SOURCE (-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE) _chk variants. Keyed underscore-stripped so __memcpy_chk etc. resolve here (lookup_model strips leading underscores). The extra trailing destlen/objsize args are compile-time guards, not data flow. Copy/concat use the 'fortified_overflow' class: the call still aborts at runtime, so it is lower-severity than the raw variant but a tainted length/source reaching it is worth surfacing. Format _chk variants live in the format section (they also carry 'varargs').

sink.detail: attacker-controlled length to __memcpy_chk (fortified; aborts at runtime)
attacker-controlled length to __memmove_chk (fortified; aborts at runtime)
attacker-controlled length to __memset_chk (fortified; aborts at runtime)
unbounded copy of tainted source into __strcpy_chk dest (fortified; aborts at runtime)
unbounded copy via __stpcpy_chk (fortified; aborts at runtime)
attacker-controlled length to __strncpy_chk (fortified; aborts at runtime)
unbounded append of tainted source into __strcat_chk dest (fortified; aborts at runtime)
attacker-controlled length to __strncat_chk (fortified; aborts at runtime)

models._comment_annex_k: C11 Annex-K / 'secure CRT' *_s variants. A destsz/bufsz guard arg follows the destination, shifting src/count/format one position right vs the classic libc functions: the copy family is (dest, destsz, src[, count]); the printf family is (buffer, bufsz, format, ...). They are bounds-checked and abort at runtime, so they reuse the lower-severity fortified_* classes of the __*_chk family. Positions follow the Annex-K signatures (NOT the Microsoft _snprintf_s(...,count,...) form) and were verified against real 32-bit ARM callsites.

sink.detail: attacker-controlled count to memcpy_s (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
attacker-controlled count to memmove_s (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
attacker-controlled count to memset_s (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
tainted source into strcpy_s dest (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
attacker-controlled count to strncpy_s (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
tainted source into strcat_s dest (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
attacker-controlled count to strncat_s (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
tainted format/args into sprintf_s (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
tainted format/args into snprintf_s (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)
tainted format into vsnprintf_s (bounds-checked; aborts at runtime)

models._comment_optional_sinks: Opt-in sinks: a sink with 'optional': true fires only when its 'class' is passed via --sink-class (engine: enabled_sink_classes). Off by default so 'tainted data written out' does not spam normal runs; useful when auditing persistence / file corruption / exfiltration. They are still non-empty models, so they suppress the conservative 'unmodeled external' fallback exactly like the benign {} entries they replace.

sink.detail: tainted data (arg0) or size/count (args1-2) written via fwrite
tainted data (arg1) or length (arg2) written via write()
tainted data (arg1) or length (arg2) sent via send()
tainted data (arg1) or length (arg2) sent via sendto()

models._comment_glib: GLib (glib-2.0) allocator / dup / list helpers, common on parser paths. Without models these surface as unmodeled_callee frontier leaves and flood output (#160). Allocators mirror malloc/calloc/realloc (alloc_size sink on the byte-count arg); g_free/g_slice_free are benign. The g_str*/g_memdup helpers return a freshly-allocated copy (propagate source -> *ret); g_strlcpy/g_strlcat are size-bounded copies (propagate, no overflow sink). List helpers store the data pointer into the container (propagate the data arg -> ret).
models._comment_benign: Empty models mark functions that neither source, propagate, nor sink taint, so a tainted argument does not trigger the conservative 'unmodeled external' fallback. They cut noise without hiding real flows.
models._comment_byteorder: Byte-order and address conversions TRANSFORM their input into their return value, so taint MUST flow arg->ret. Modeling them benign ({}) let an attacker-controlled length laundered through `n = ntohl(hdr->len)` drop to untainted before reaching `memcpy(dst, src, n)`, producing a false all-clear on the most common network-parse overflow. htons/htonl/ntohs/ntohl take a scalar; inet_addr derives its result from the string it is passed.
